sourceOccurrences.label: Finite-size scaling and random graphs
sourceOccurrences.note: Critical windows on finite graphs require definitions distinct from infinite-cluster thresholds.

proofUses.reason: The root cluster of 6WC8 at a uniform root is the component containing it, which is the component of size |C_i| with probability |C_i|/n.
Averaging the conditional identity CY0D over configurations gives the averaged susceptibility of 8DSI.
The row sum of G(n,p) is (n-1)p, and the uniform row-sum bound gives the susceptibility bound at every root, hence for the average.
Markov's inequality for the largest squared component, bounded by the second component moment of XCGS, combined with the susceptibility bound MIQ7.

With theta = lambda the window is that of 38XP, which gives the two-sided bound for L_1 and the upper bound for every L_j <= L_1. For j >= 2, the Y0FX tails bound the mean of the vertex count in components of size between n^{2/3}/A and n^{2/3}, the 25Z4 distinct-cluster comparison and the TUD2 root-sum identity bound its variance, and Chebyshev's inequality gives at least j such components.
